intelligence.title: The Same Law, Everywhere

intelligence.essence: Two rules that look like two are one law. In Project Intelligence, every area links to the relevant places in the apps. In the apps, every top bar carries its related apps as quick tabs. Underneath both is the same law: one thing lives in one place, and everything it matters to links to it — the Link Law, running as navigation, running as record-keeping, running everywhere. A system that obeys one organizing law on every surface stays coherent as it grows, and the user never has to do the organizing themselves: it was all thought out for them, in advance.
intelligence.human_view: It arrived as a small correction. Shawn was separating two apps in his mind: the Dashboard is numbers and graphs; Reports is written intelligence, a letter about your life. Related, but different — so, he said, each should carry a button to the other, right there in the top bar. Then he saw it widen: not just those two — every app. The top bar of any app should carry the areas related to it, the places a person standing there would want to go next, matched by intent, not by org chart. And then he saw the floor under both thoughts: it is the same logic he had already given for Project Intelligence, where every area carries links to the relevant places in the apps. One law, two coats — then every coat. The system is continuously, proactively, intelligently organizing itself around the person: everything laid out, everything thought out for them, so the experience is convenience that feels like intelligence — because it is. His name for what it adds up to: the best possible experience of the internet. The new net. Not a hit at Google or Facebook — a new experience entirely, one that hasn't been possible until now, because it takes an intelligent system to do the organizing.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a treehouse with lots of little rooms. In a normal treehouse, every time you want a different room, you climb all the way down and all the way back up. Exhausting! But in this treehouse, every room has little doors straight to the rooms you visit from there. In the snack room, there's a door to the games room. In the games room, a door back. Everything still has its own one room — the snacks live in the snack room, nowhere else — but every room points to its friends. You never wander. You never get lost. Wherever you are standing, the next place you'd want is already right there.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like a well-kept kitchen, dear. In my mother's house, the recipe cards lived in one box — just one, never copies scattered in drawers. But on the pantry shelf, right where the flour was, there was a little note: "the card box is by the window." And on the card box: "flour, top shelf." Everything in its one true place, and everything pointing to what it's used with. That's all this law is, dressed in new clothes: one home for every thing, and a kind word of directions wherever you'd naturally look next. A house — or a network — organized like that never makes you feel stupid for not knowing where things are. It did the remembering for you.
intelligence.naya_view: For every Naya, as an operating rule. **One law, every surface — do not mint local variants of it.** (1) ONE HOME: a thing lives in exactly one place. A copy where a link belongs is a defect — in content, in records, in principles alike. (2) LINK WHAT IT MATTERS TO: when you build, fill, or file anything, name its relatives — every place it matters to — and link them, in the same pass. In Project Intelligence: every area's record links to the relevant app surfaces and sibling records. In the apps: every top bar carries the app's related areas as quick tabs. (3) CHOOSE RELATIVES BY INTENT: the test is "what would the person standing here want next?" — never the org chart, never the folder structure. (4) A THING THAT MATTERS WITH NO LINK IS A DEFECT, the same class as a dead button: it exists, it matters, and it is unreachable from where it is needed. (5) WHEN A RULE SURFACES TWICE, FIND THE ONE LAW: do not file two rules and let them drift apart; name the single law underneath and cite it in both places. Tonight's evidence: the bar law was filed as its own canon note (SN-1906, Power) and the Project Intelligence linking rule has stood in the record for days — this note exists because Shawn recognized, live, that they were never two. First pair under the law: Reports ⇄ Dashboard — a Dashboard button in Reports, a Reports button in the Dashboard, both ways, by design.
intelligence.ai_view: This is a note about what kind of system NayaNET is. The old internet is organized around the provider: their structure, their maze, their business — and the user does all the adapting, forever. An intelligent network inverts that. The system does the thinking in advance, continuously and proactively, organizing itself around the person's intent, so that wherever a person stands, what they need next is already within reach. That is why the unity of the law matters more than either instance of it: a law that shows up in the records, in the navigation, and in the linking is not three design decisions — it is the physics of the system. Physics doesn't drift. When the same law governs every surface, the whole system becomes learnable in one lesson and predictable everywhere, for the citizens inside it and for the Nayas who build it: wherever you are, the way to what matters is already there. Shawn's verdict on why it couldn't exist before is the deepest line in it: a network organized around the person requires the organizer to be intelligent. Now the organizer is.
